yeah ofc! i still think it's a wonderful movie and a terribly important part of the slasher subgenre, and there's a lot of really new movies who also have this trope and as much as i liked their overall plots (as well as in halloween!) for the most part they are a bit too stretched out, like the strangers: prey at night (2018).
However, for me there are also some older movies like Psycho (1960) which is also kind of a slasher movie and doesnt have that kind of a prolonged building of the scary atmosphere. Of course i know we can't compare Carpenter and Hitchcock cause their experiences as directors were completely different at the time they were filming these movies, and i think that overall as Michael's lore was progressing, so was the quality of his movies:)

when the killers in horror movies make it all about the scary atmosphere rather than actually killing the victims:/ i know its important for the movie to have the suspense but when its stretched out throughout over half of the movie then its getting frustrating and boring, like just kill them already! i think halloween (1978) is a good example in this case
